question: [SAMPLE FIXTURE] How do the SoloScale Resume API and Resume Cloud worker protect requests and paid model calls?

chunks.text: Why did oversized Resume API requests come back as HTTP 400 instead of 413?

A receive-time body-limit exception surfaced as a FastAPI 400. The repair is a bounded ASGI pre-reader that counts each streamed request chunk and returns 413 before FastAPI buffers or parses JSON. It does not trust the Content-Length header.
Verification: the API test suite passed, and a request over the complete body budget returned 413 with a stable error envelope and no input body in the response.
A lease-expired RUNNING task becomes NEEDS_REVIEW and is never requeued, because a paid provider may already have received the model call.
The worker claims queued tasks with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and permits exactly one attempt per task.
Every declared claim must cite an in-context chunk retrieved in the same Evidence Agent run.
Cited chunk hashes are rechecked against the current knowledge index before a candidate result is accepted.
The local operator UI binds only to the loopback address 127.0.0.1 on port 8765.

claims.text: The Resume API rejects an oversized request with 413 by counting streamed chunks before JSON parsing, without trusting Content-Length.
The body-limit repair was verified: an over-budget request returned 413 with a stable error envelope.
Resume Cloud never requeues a lease-expired task, because the paid provider may already have been called.
The Evidence Agent accepts a claim only when it cites an in-context chunk from the same run.
The local operator UI listens only on 127.0.0.1:8765.
